comment: Built-in catalog of local ACP agents offered by Tools > External ACP Agent.
Read by Scripts/acp_catalog.py, which flattens it to TSV for the shell library.
note is USER FACING and appears in the dialog's info pane. Keep it to what someone running
Cadabra on their own machine can act on - what the agent is, what it needs, how to get it.
Do NOT write our own provenance into it: phrases like "verified here" or "not probed here"
mean a developer's machine, which is nothing the user can see or check.
verification is OURS. acp_catalog.py never emits it, so it cannot reach the UI. It records
what we actually confirmed and how, and which rows are still NOT PROBED - the intent being
to probe every pre-configured tool, so this doubles as the list of what is still owed.
A row is a STARTING POINT for the command field, never a promise. The dialog probes whatever
argv it is about to store, and the probe's answer is what gets believed. Two rows went stale
during development, both of them rows nobody had run.
Fields: id is persisted in the user's settings, so DO NOT rename one - it would orphan an
existing selection. args is a list, so an agent that takes no arguments is [] rather than
the single space the old tab-separated table needed. url is the vendor's own information
page, shown as a clickable link; every one was verified to resolve.
Rows are ordered alphabetically by label, with Custom pinned last, because the dialog renders
them in file order. Order carries no meaning: the selection is keyed by id, so rows can be
resorted freely.
The five rows from the ACP registry (Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Mistral Vibe, Qwen Code)
come from https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json, which is
machine readable and carries each agent's distribution details. That registry is also the
cheapest way to check whether these rows have gone stale.
The custom row is not an agent and has no vendor, so its url is not a product page: it points
at the registry of ACP agents, which is what someone about to type a command is looking for.
selection.changed.sh gives that row a different link LABEL for the same reason.

agents.label: Claude Code (ACP adapter)
agents.summary: An adapter that exposes Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK to any ACP client.
agents.note: Claude Code speaks no ACP itself; this adapter wraps it. It needs no login of its own - it uses your existing Claude Code credentials.
agents.verification: Probed: initialize ok at 0.69.0, protocolVersion 1, loadSession, authMethods empty. Takes no arguments - src/index.ts falls through to runAcp() with zero args. npm bin claude-agent-acp.

agents.label: Codex (ACP adapter)
agents.summary: An adapter that exposes OpenAI's Codex coding assistant to any ACP client.
agents.note: OpenAI's Codex speaks no ACP itself; this adapter wraps it. Install the npm package @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp, which provides the codex-acp command.
agents.verification: NOT PROBED. ACP registry 1.4.0, npx distribution with no args; bin name codex-acp confirmed from npm package metadata.

agents.label: Cursor
agents.summary: Cursor's coding agent, driven through its cursor-agent command line tool.
agents.note: Cursor's installer provides this as both agent and cursor-agent, and its documentation uses agent acp. Needs a Cursor account.
agents.verification: NOT PROBED. ACP registry 2026.08.11, binary distribution: cmd cursor-agent, args [acp]. Cursor's live installer at cursor.com/install symlinks BOTH ~/.local/bin/agent (which it comments as primary) and ~/.local/bin/cursor-agent (legacy) to the same executable, and cursor.com/docs/cli/acp uses agent acp throughout with zero occurrences of cursor-agent. We look for cursor-agent ON PURPOSE: a PATH lookup for a name as generic as agent can match an unrelated binary and report Ready for the wrong tool, which is a risk today, whereas the legacy symlink being dropped is a risk later and would only show up as Not found. Revisit if Cursor stops creating it.

agents.label: Gemini
agents.summary: Google's Gemini CLI, which speaks ACP as a documented mode and is listed in the ACP Agent Registry.
agents.note: Google's site warns that unpaid-tier and Google One users are moved to Antigravity CLI, with paid and enterprise access continuing, so check before relying on it.
agents.verification: NOT PROBED. --acp confirmed in google-gemini/gemini-cli packages/cli/src/config/config.ts; --experimental-acp still functions but is declared deprecated. Banner read from geminicli.com, which the official README links as its docs site.

agents.label: GitHub Copilot
agents.summary: GitHub's AI pair programmer, as a command line agent.
agents.note: Install the npm package @github/copilot, which provides the copilot command. Needs a GitHub Copilot subscription.
agents.verification: NOT PROBED. ACP registry 1.0.80, npx distribution with args [--acp]; bin name copilot confirmed from npm package metadata.

agents.label: Grok
agents.summary: xAI's terminal coding agent, now branded Grok Build; the installed binary identifies itself as Grok Build TUI.
agents.note: A successful test names no agent, because Grok reports no agent information. May need its own login - it uses grok.com and a cached token.
agents.verification: Probed: initialize ok, protocolVersion 1, no agentInfo. The installed binary's --help identifies it as Grok Build TUI.

agents.label: Kilo
agents.summary: An open source, model-agnostic AI coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal.
agents.note: A node script rather than a binary, so it only starts if node is available. May need its own login (kilo auth login) before prompts work.

agents.label: Kimi Code
agents.summary: A terminal coding agent from Moonshot AI, shipped as a single binary rather than through npm.
agents.note: Needs a login first - kimi acp --login runs a device-code flow. Moonshot ships it as a single binary from its own installer rather than through npm.
agents.verification: NOT PROBED. Invocation taken from the tool's own kimi acp --help, supplied from a machine where it is installed; cross-checked against MoonshotAI/kimi-code.

agents.label: Mistral Vibe
agents.note: Installing mistral-vibe provides a SEPARATE vibe-acp command alongside the main vibe CLI, and vibe-acp is the ACP entry point.
agents.verification: PARTLY PROBED at 2.0.1: initialize ok as mistral-vibe, protocolVersion 1, no auth methods; session/new then failed with a bare Internal error, against an install 24 minor versions behind the registry's 2.24.1, so that says little about the current release. Console scripts vibe / vibe-acp / vibe-app-server confirmed from pyproject.toml.

agents.label: OpenCode
agents.summary: An open source AI coding agent that runs in the terminal, from Anomaly.
agents.note: May need its own login (opencode auth login) before prompts work.
agents.verification: Probed: initialize ok as OpenCode 1.17.13, loadSession, MCP http+sse.

agents.label: Qwen Code
agents.note: Install the npm package @qwen-code/qwen-code, which provides the qwen command.
agents.verification: NOT PROBED. ACP registry 0.21.12; bin name qwen confirmed from npm metadata. The registry also passes --experimental-skills, which Qwen's own config.ts marks Deprecated, ignored and hidden, so it is left out.

agents.label: Custom
agents.summary: Anything else that speaks the Agent Client Protocol over stdio.
agents.note: Type the full command and arguments yourself.
agents.verification: Not an agent - there is no invocation to verify.
